sections.heading: 1. Respect for rights
sections.html: Wody respects copyright, trademarks and other intellectual property. Third-party games, studios, brands and artists own their works. Using a work in Wody does not give you or Wody any right to it.

sections.heading: 2. What Wody does not do
sections.html: Wody does not run a gallery of third-party artwork, does not bundle official artwork of games or studios, does not scrape such artwork and does not sell it. Themes and scenes provided by Wody are original and drawn by Wody.

sections.heading: 3. Your responsibility
sections.html: If you upload or link an image or a song, you must have the necessary rights or another lawful basis. Each time you publish or edit your public profile you confirm this, and you accept the policies, by ticking an unchecked box, and before uploading a song you confirm separately that you own it or have the rights holder’s permission. The confirmation is your statement. It is not a guarantee and it does not make unauthorized use lawful. You alone are responsible for the music you upload or link.

sections.heading: 4. Reporting a possible infringement
sections.html:
Use the Copyright complaint form. Please give: your name or organization, a way to contact you, a description of the protected work, a link or other identification of the original work if available, the profile or customization where you found the material, why you believe it infringes, and your confirmation that the information is accurate and that you are authorized to act.

We do not ask for a postal address unless the law requires it. Your contact details are not shown to the user concerned.

sections.heading: 5. How a complaint is handled
sections.html:
1. The complaint is recorded and the content is identified.
  2. The operator reviews it. If it is unclear, we may ask you for clarification.
  3. If the notice is sufficiently precise and the content appears unlawful, access to the content is disabled or the content is removed.
  4. The uploader sees a notice and can appeal.
  5. The decision, its reason and the time are recorded.

Wody does not promise a fixed removal deadline. Where the law requires specific steps, those steps apply.

sections.heading: 6. Repeat violations
sections.html: Confirmed violations are counted. Repeated violations can lead to a suspension of customization, or to the suspension or block of the Discord account linked to the profile for Wody features.

sections.heading: 7. Appeals and counter-notices
sections.html: The user whose content was disabled can explain why the use is lawful through the appeal on the profile page tab. Wody reviews it and may restore the content or keep it disabled. Wody does not restore content automatically after a fixed time. Images that are only linked are not stored by Wody: they stay visible only while the link remains valid on the hosting platform.

sections.heading: 8. Limits
sections.html: Wody cannot detect every infringement. Reports and review are the main way problems are found. This procedure is not described as compliant with any specific foreign law. Which legal regime applies to Wody, and the exact obligations that follow, must be confirmed by a qualified Romanian or EU lawyer.

sections.heading: 1. Purpose
sections.html: This policy explains how the Wody Battle Pass works and which data it uses. It applies to the Global Battle Pass and to server Battle Passes created by owners of Premium servers.

sections.heading: 2. Seasons and priority
sections.html: A Global season is run by Wody. A server season is run by the owner of a Premium server. When a Global season is active, it takes priority and server seasons are held back without losing their settings or progress. A server season needs an active Premium subscription for the server.

sections.heading: 3. Data we use
sections.html: We store counters needed to run a season: XP, level, claimed rewards, quest and achievement progress, and items you earned. We do not store the text of your messages or any voice audio. Message and voice activity is converted to counters at the moment it happens.

sections.heading: 4. Fair use
sections.html: XP is protected by cooldowns, limits, duplicate and spam detection and AFK rules. Attempts to inflate progress, such as repeated messages, automation or alternate accounts, are not counted. Owners can see aggregated figures only.

sections.heading: 5. Rewards
sections.html: Rewards are digital items shown on your Wody profile and Passport. They have no cash value and cannot be bought, sold or transferred. Wody does not sell Battle Pass levels or progress.

sections.heading: 6. Your choices
sections.html: You decide which items appear in your profile showcase. You can stop earning XP by leaving a server or by not taking part. To ask about your data, use the contact details at the end of this page.

sections.heading: 7. Changes
sections.html: Seasons can be paused, ended or archived by their owner. Rewards you already earned stay on your Passport. We may update this policy; the version and date are shown above.

battlepassHelp.title: Battle Pass help
battlepassHelp.intro: The Wody Battle Pass turns activity in your Discord servers into seasonal progress with levels, rewards, quests and badges. This page explains how it works and answers the most common questions.

steps.title: Earn XP
steps.text: Send messages and spend time in voice channels. Each source has its own cooldowns and daily limits, so steady activity counts and spam does not.

steps.title: Reach levels
steps.text: XP fills your level bar. Every season defines its own number of levels and how much XP each one needs.

steps.title: Claim rewards
steps.text: Rewards unlock at their level. Open the Battle Pass page, sign in with Discord and claim them. A reward can be claimed only once.

steps.title: Complete quests and achievements
steps.text: Quests give bonus XP. Achievements unlock when all their conditions are met. Collections group rewards and can grant an extra reward.

steps.title: Show your items
steps.text: Badges and other items you earn appear on your Wody Passport. You choose which ones appear in your profile showcase.

faq.q: What is the Global Battle Pass?
faq.a: It is a season run by Wody that works on every server where the bot is present. Everyone progresses in the same season.

faq.q: What is a server Battle Pass?
faq.a: Owners of Premium servers can run their own seasons with their own levels, rewards and page design. It is available on that server only.

faq.q: Why is my server Battle Pass not running?
faq.a: While a Global season is active it takes priority. Your server seasons keep their settings and progress and resume when the Global season ends.

faq.q: How is XP earned and limited?
faq.a: XP comes from counted messages and from voice time. Cooldowns, daily, weekly and season limits, duplicate and spam protection and AFK rules apply to every season.

faq.q: Does Wody store my messages or voice audio?
faq.a: No. Only counters such as XP, level and claimed rewards are stored. Message text and voice audio are never saved.

faq.q: Why was my reward claim refused?
faq.a: The reward may not be unlocked yet, may already be claimed, may have expired, or the season may be closed. The page shows the exact reason.

faq.q: Can a reward be claimed twice?
faq.a: No. Each reward is claimed once per member and season, even if you click several times or use two devices.

faq.q: How do I show my items on my profile?
faq.a: Open the Battle Pass page, go to Showcase and choose the items to show. Your Wody Passport lists the badges you have earned.

faq.q: What is a season page?
faq.a: Each Battle Pass season can have its own public page with the season’s real levels, rewards, quests, countdown and leaderboard. The Owner designs and publishes it, and it only shows data the season really has.

faq.q: Who can see my progress on a season page?
faq.a: Only you. When you sign in with Discord the page shows your own level, XP and claimed rewards. Other members never see your private progress, and a server season page never shows data from another server.

cheat.a: Each message is judged once, even when many arrive together. Too many messages, repeated wrong input and robot-like timing lead to short pauses. Nobody is banned or kicked by Counting.

mistake.a: Each server chooses: restart from the beginning, go back to the last milestone, keep counting or only warn. Strikes, short locks and saves can soften or sharpen the result.

privacy.a: Counters, records, streaks and rewards. Message text, attachments and audio are never stored. Public pages show names and numbers only, and only for games a server made public.

access.a: By default only members who can manage the server. The owner can let everyone open /statistics, and then members see only the overview, activity and growth sections. The dashboard is always limited to people who can manage the server.

accuracy.a: Message counts are exact for the days Wody was collecting; days without collection are shown as gaps, never as zero. Participants are estimates and the member curve is rebuilt from observed joins and leaves. The module is designed to store as little as possible, but it does not claim to make your server compliant with GDPR or any other law by itself.
accuracy.q: How accurate are the numbers and is this GDPR compliant?

classes.a: Channels are classed as Very Active, Active, Moderate, Low Activity or Inactive by their average messages per day. The defaults are 50, 10, 2 and 0.25, and you can change all four limits on the dashboard.
classes.q: What are the channel activity classes?

participants.a: Wody feeds a salted one-way hash of each author into a small probabilistic sketch (HyperLogLog). The sketch can estimate how many different people wrote, but it cannot be turned back into names or IDs. The estimate has a typical error of a few percent.
participants.q: How are participants counted without storing who wrote?

privacy.a: Stored: messages per channel, day and hour, and a salted sketch that estimates how many different people wrote. Never stored: message text, attachments, member IDs, names, avatars or profiles. Deleting the data replaces the salt.
privacy.q: What is stored and what is not?

retention.a: You choose a retention period between 30 and 365 days, 90 by default, and older counters are removed automatically. You can also delete every counter at any time from the dashboard or from /statistics in Discord.
retention.q: How long are counters kept and can I delete them?

score.a: A number from 0 to 100 from five factors: member growth (25%), participation (25%), stability (20%), spread across channels (15%) and channel vitality (15%). A factor without data is left out and the rest are rescaled. It needs at least 14 days of data. It reads counters; it does not say how good a community is.

meta.title: Wody Themes: how website themes and effects work
meta.description: Learn how Wody themes style your server pages, which scenes and effects are available, and how to turn effects off.

themesHelp.lead: Themes change how your server’s public pages look on the Wody website: colors, scenes and effects. They never change how the bot or your Discord server works.

how.title: How it works
how.body: Wody offers official themes (Miami Neon, Synthwave, Aurora, Cosmos, Sakura and Midnight Ocean) and can add seasonal or event themes. You pick one, adjust it, preview it and publish it. Each server has its own settings, so a change on your server never affects another server.

who.title: Who can change what
who.basic: Themes are a Premium feature. Servers without Premium keep the standard look. Dashboard > Premium > Theme Studio.
who.premium: Premium servers (Dashboard > Premium > Theme Studio) get all palette colors, a gradient, glass and blur, border, shadow and navigation styles, ambient lighting, animation strength, background movement, particle density, layout density, a choice of scenes, up to three custom sections, a logo and a custom banner image link.
who.owner: Global themes, their images and publishing schedule are managed only by the Wody Owner. Servers cannot edit or replace them.

intro.title: Scenes and effects
intro.body: Every theme is built from a scene (a neon sunset, a synthwave grid, an aurora, a starry cosmos, a cherry blossom dusk or a moonlit ocean) and a set of soft effects such as stars, neon streaks, petals, bubbles or snow. Colors, scene and effects can all be changed with Premium. Effects are light, slow and never flash.

access.title: Accessibility and performance
access.body: Text colors are checked for contrast, so a theme or server cannot make text unreadable. Visitors who prefer reduced motion see a still scene. Every visitor can turn effects and animations off, pick a quality level (Low, Medium, High, Ultra) or let Wody choose. Lightning is always soft and slow, safe for people sensitive to light. If a page runs slowly, effects switch off automatically and the still background stays. If an image cannot load, the page falls back to the standard look.

assets.title: Images and licensing
assets.body: Backgrounds and logos are separate, optimized image files, not code drawings. Every image carries a license record and is checked for format, size and dimensions. SVG files, scripts and executables are rejected. Images are stored as files; the database only keeps references.

safe.title: Safety
safe.body: Themes contain only fixed choices, colors and numbers. No JavaScript, CSS or HTML can be added, and a theme can never touch other servers, permissions, sign-in or security. Every change by the Owner or a server manager is recorded in an audit log with who, what, when and the result.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.q1: Does a theme change how the bot works?
faq.a1: No. Themes only change how your public pages on the Wody website look.
faq.q2: What do the themes look like?
faq.a2: Each official theme is a scene of light and atmosphere, such as a neon sunset or a night ocean, with soft moving effects. There are no characters.
faq.q3: How do I turn the animations off?
faq.a3: Open the theme settings button at the bottom of the page and switch off Visual effects and Animations, or set your device to reduced motion.
faq.q4: Can I upload my own logo?
faq.a4: Yes, with Premium. A Premium server can upload its own logo (PNG, JPEG or WebP up to 1 MB), pick another scene, link to a banner image on a secure address and add short custom sections.
faq.a5: Your Premium theme settings are kept but only the basic ones are shown to visitors. They apply again if Premium comes back.
faq.q6: Who can publish a theme on my server?
faq.a6: Only people who can manage your Discord server. Wody checks this with Discord every time.
